sections.title: Executive Verdict
sections.text: Credent has built a diagnostic-logistics and outsourced-services operation, but its apparent FY26 leap mixes acquisitions, organic execution and a materially corrected prior-year revenue base. Consolidated sales were ₹214.16 crore and profit about ₹18.36 crore, while operating cash was negative ₹6.62 crore. The fresh IPO provides meaningful resources but most proceeds fund working capital, not surplus cash. This is a completed conditional review, not a purchase recommendation: constant-parent growth REV is scored from recovered restated history, while expected return R remains NS. The funded base sensitivity produces roughly 1.2% annual return from the dated ₹340.10 quote, well below a 15% hurdle.

sections.title: Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text: Review date: 20 October 2026. Identity: Credent Connect N Care Limited, ISIN INE1KPX01025, NSE Emerge symbol CREDENT; listed-period observations begin 20 August 2026. The 19 October official close is ₹340.10, not a live executable price. Final prospectus dated 18 August and FY26 annual financials establish the financial perimeter. FY24–FY25 restated figures are standalone; FY26 includes acquired subsidiaries. Historical and constant-parent growth confidence are medium; consolidated organic decomposition and post-IPO funding confidence remain low. There is no automatic G2 hold for disclosed restatements and no automatic governance failure from an old, resolved disqualification.

sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text: Supported analyst factors are GOV 4, MOAT 5, REV 8, DUR 7, CAP 4, CASH 4, BAL 5, EXEC 5 and EARN 5. BQS is 5.14 and Growth Quality GQS is 6.35. REV uses 32.62% three-year constant-parent CAGR and the short-history cap of 8, not acquired group growth. R remains NS because conditional financing and earnings assumptions cannot yet be adopted as expected return. D 3, P 4 and L 7 describe downside, asset support and dated tradability. IAS remains NS with exact unreweighted coverage and bounds. No persistent low-CAP/CASH cap is asserted from one acquired-scope year.

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text: The group combines diagnostic sample logistics, outsourced operations, healthcare field services, marketing and technology support. FY26 service revenue includes logistics ₹54.11 crore, operations/supply-chain ₹53.38 crore and healthcare ₹92.18 crore; SaaS is only ₹2.05 crore. This is therefore predominantly a people-and-process service business, not a high-margin pure software platform. The prospectus describes 2,530 diagnostic partners at March 2026, 97 commercial vehicles and 2,589 riders at June end, and a wider workforce of 6,338 including healthcare contract personnel. These measures have different dates and populations and are not added together. Collection route density and client integration matter, but payment approval and payroll timing control cash economics.

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text: Partner relationships, routing know-how and outsourced workflow integration offer moderate switching friction. They do not eliminate price competition or confer guaranteed volumes. TeamLease is a useful staffing-economics comparator, not a direct diagnostic-logistics valuation peer: its FY26 consolidated sales were ₹11,790.67 crore and owner profit ₹139.69 crore, much thinner profit per revenue than Credent. TeamLease CFO of ₹301.80 crore included ₹120.91 crore net tax refunds; cash capex was ₹29.45 crore. That refund must not be extrapolated as normal cash conversion. Its scale and different service mix make copying its P/E inappropriate. Diagnostic laboratory owners are also imperfect peers because they own testing capability and consumer brands, whereas Credent largely supports delivery and field operations. No unsupported peer-price premium is used.

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text: Restated standalone revenue was ₹75.7332 crore in FY24 and ₹77.9426 crore in FY25. FY26 parent standalone revenue was ₹139.3887 crore; consolidated revenue was ₹214.1618 crore. Healthcare came under control in April 2025 and became wholly owned in October; Team was acquired in December and Alltrak in February 2026. Consequently the group increase is not organic CAGR. FY25 statutory revenue of ₹81.8232 crore was restated downward by ₹3.8805 crore, principally unbilled-service timing; statutory PAT ₹5.5323 crore became restated ₹2.2467 crore after revenue, tax, depreciation and other adjustments. An older issuer DRHP supplies restated FY23 parent revenue of ₹59.7537 crore. The FY23–FY26 constant-parent CAGR is therefore 32.62% and is scoreable separately from acquired group growth. Original FY21 and FY22 scans verify statutory revenue of ₹17.5385 crore and ₹35.9034 crore; their five-year endpoint CAGR of 51.37% is diagnostic only because the older statutory-to-restated bridge is incomplete. FY21 is also a depressed pandemic base. Parent growth is not a same-customer organic cohort, and related-party service mix changed as subsidiaries were acquired. Top-one/five/ten customers contribute 15.76%/59.05%/81.76% of FY26 revenue, so loss of a few contracts matters more than a large partner-count headline.

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text: The IPO issued 49.68 lakh fresh shares at ₹189, raising ₹93.8952 crore gross and ₹81.7242 crore net, with no offer-for-sale cash credited to the company. Objects allocate ₹63.8 crore to working capital, ₹3 crore machinery, ₹6 crore debt repayment and ₹8.9242 crore general corporate purposes. Working-capital allocation is ₹29.5 crore in FY27 and ₹34.3 crore in FY28. The model releases this cash only against incremental requirements and excludes unused reserves from terminal free cash. Acquisitions consumed ₹10.84 crore net cash in FY26 and produced ₹2.35 crore goodwill. Acquisition-date opening balances prevent a simple year-end receivable change from being called organic reinvestment. Incremental ROIC is therefore not assigned a precise comparable percentage. Growth needs customer collections and productive staffing, not merely more invoiced sales.

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text: Promoters retain 63.66% after the IPO. Related loans and service transactions require close monitoring, but subsidiary balances are not automatically external promoter diversion: Alltrak receivables of ₹3.7417 crore and loans of ₹2.8524 crore are eliminated in consolidation after control. Director loans of ₹9.44024 crore converted into shares in October 2025 are noncash financing; the later 50:1 bonus is not a cash inflow. Earlier audit emphasis concerned formal internal-control documentation; management reported formalisation and FY26 carries no such emphasis. The 18 September CFO resignation cites personal reasons and an immediate replacement, not an asserted accounting dispute. The September auditor appointment is for five years and is not an auditor resignation. The prospectus discloses that promoter/non-executive director Ashok Kumar Sharma appeared on a 2016–2021 disqualification list after a predecessor subsidiary failed to file for three years, and states DIN reapproval in December 2019 and no present disqualification. This historical disclosure is not evidence of a current ban or criminal finding. The prospectus also discloses cash-flow attachments omitted from AOC-4 filings for FY2016–FY2024 and historical chit-fund investments that it says have since been fully withdrawn. These dated disclosures reinforce controls scrutiny; neither is presented as a current loss or an allegation of intentional misconduct.

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text: FY26 group CFO reconciles PBT ₹24.2019 crore plus depreciation, interest and other noncash adjustments to ₹29.235 crore before working capital. Receivables consumed ₹28.3561 crore, payables ₹3.4214 crore and tax ₹5.6636 crore, partly offset by other liabilities. CFO was negative ₹6.6233 crore and cash capex ₹5.5135 crore, producing negative ₹12.1368 crore FCF before acquisitions. Group debt was ₹21.9475 crore, cash ₹2.2102 crore, equity ₹43.7907 crore and noncurrent FD ₹2.2221 crore, excluded from free cash pending restrictions. Receivables ₹58.8273 crore include ₹8.7455 crore unbilled revenue; billing approval is a revenue-recognition risk addressed by audit sampling and subsequent invoices, not proof of collectability. Standalone CFO includes a deposit outflow: reclassifying the ₹2.2221 crore FD would improve standalone CFO and worsen investing cash equally, leaving total cash unchanged; group FD is already investing and must not be adjusted twice. Alltrak full-year PAT and the shorter consolidated contribution are different periods, not an issuer inconsistency. The disclosed ₹0.6211 crore GST dispute is contingent, not a proven operating loss.

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text: At ₹340.10 and 1.82229 crore post-IPO shares, market capitalisation is approximately ₹619.77 crore, about 33.75 times FY26 consolidated reported profit. This static multiple mixes pre-IPO earnings with post-IPO shares and is not a forecast. Fully linked bear/base/bull cases use revenue growth 8%/14%/22%, EBITDA margins 10%/12.5%/14%, operating NWC 35%/30%/25% of sales, interest 11%/10%/9% and terminal EV/EBITDA 8/11/14. Each year links tax, capex, reserve release, borrowing, repayment and a ₹3 crore cash floor. Conditional terminal prices are ₹169/₹361/₹689, giving approximately −13.1%/1.2%/15.2% five-year annual returns. The base 15% hurdle entry is about ₹179. These are sensitivities, not price targets: actual post-IPO deployment and recurring acquired earnings remain unresolved. Unused IPO reserves and noncurrent FD receive no terminal cash credit. New draws incur half-year interest, with ordinary repayments at year-end; tax, interest and borrowing are solved jointly.

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text: A large client can reduce volumes without a minimum-volume commitment while field payroll and supplier obligations continue. Delayed approval of unbilled work can then absorb the IPO buffer, forcing expensive borrowing or dilution. The severe case combines shrinking sales, a 7% margin, 45% NWC, 13% interest and no available IPO reserve; it is deliberately not presented as the most likely forecast. Separate tests cover aged-receivable loss, slower collections, lower margins, project overruns and 10% dilution without assumed proceeds. Earlier restatements and control gaps justify monitoring but do not establish fraud. Sanctioned borrowing limits, post-issue cash and tax-case status would determine whether a stressed financing need becomes unfinanceable. With half-year interest on new draws, this severe case requires peak debt of ₹67.54 crore and produces a terminal price of ₹6.23, an annualized return of approximately −55.07%. These are stress outputs, not expected outcomes.

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text: A fivefold or tenfold share price at unchanged shares would require equity values of roughly ₹3,099 crore or ₹6,198 crore. At an illustrative 20× terminal P/E and 8% net margin, that implies revenue about ₹1,937 crore or ₹3,874 crore, respectively, versus ₹214 crore now. Such an expansion is not supported by the base model and would require a much larger deployed workforce, customer base, collection system and funding pool. New shares increase the required business value. Software optionality is too small and acquisition annualisation too uncertain to supply the missing economics by assumption.

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text: Track billed and unbilled receivables separately, subsequent collections and top-five customer exposure. Demand an exact bridge from FY26 acquired contribution to ongoing recurring service margins. Reconcile IPO object utilisation, restricted deposits, subsidiary funding and bank utilisation before crediting surplus cash. Monitor payroll statutory payments and whether documented control processes work in practice. Verify new related-party balances and any customer losses. Official turnover supports only a short 41-session listed history: exclude the 19 prelisting sessions rather than recording zero trades. The 600-share lot costs ₹204,060, two lots ₹408,120 and three exceed ₹5 lakh. REG1 flags fewer than 100 unique PANs in the prior 30 days and irregular SME trading; these are exchange cautions, not invented missing-trade days or evidence of wrongdoing.

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text: Research status: deep conditional review, not investment-ready. All nine quality factors are scored, with BQS 5.14 and GQS 6.35. IAS lacks a sufficiently supported R despite dated tradability evidence. No purchase action, live-exit assurance or portfolio weight is proposed. Reconsider only after post-IPO deployment and collections establish a reliable opening balance sheet, the acquired-service profit mix is normalised and valuation offers a margin of safety. A high historical growth headline alone does not satisfy those tests.

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text: Primary work covers the FY26 annual report, final prospectus, restated history, acquisitions, cash flows, related parties, capital history, IPO objects, current CFO and auditor filings, official NSE market data and decoded surveillance. The TeamLease primary report is a limited economic comparator, not a full peer valuation study. Five-year model assumptions and annual equity bridges are saved in credent_funded_model.json and embedded here, with source-linked historical anchors. Remaining material gaps are post-issue cash deployment and bank headroom, deposit restrictions, a full five-year statutory-to-restated bridge and consolidated organic/acquired decomposition, long-run customer retention and acquired software earnings recurrence. The historical director-disqualification wording and GST dispute retain their source dates and stated qualifications. Missing inputs constrain only the relevant factors and do not substitute for unperformed analysis.

valuation.formulas: Sales grow annually; EBITDA = sales × margin; depreciation = 1.5% sales; cash tax = max(0,(EBITDA - depreciation - interest) × 25%); Interest includes half-year new draws; ordinary repayments occur at year-end. CFO = EBITDA - interest - tax - change in operating NWC. FCF subtracts project and maintenance capex. IPO WC/capex reserves release only against incremental WC/project expenditure within scheduled availability, never as unrestricted surplus. Borrow to maintain 3 crore cash, then repay excess. Terminal EV = EBITDA × exit multiple. Equity = max(0,EV - debt + unrestricted cash); unused reserves and noncurrent FD excluded. IRR=(terminal price/340.1)^(1/5)-1; no dividends. New borrowing incurs half-year interest in the year drawn. Ordinary excess-cash repayments occur at year-end and receive no same-year interest saving. Curis collateral-funded FD overdraft repayment retains its explicit half-year timing. Interest, positive-profit cash tax and funding draw are solved jointly to a 1e-12 crore tolerance; new borrowing is a funding requirement, not a committed facility.

GOV.reason: Material unbilled-revenue timing restatements and earlier control-documentation gaps reduce confidence, alongside concentrated family ownership and historical filing failures. Counterevidence: timing corrections are explicitly reconciled, FY26 control emphasis is nil, related loans/conversions are disclosed, and the CFO was immediately replaced. No wrongdoing or current disqualification is inferred.

MOAT.reason: Diagnostic-partner logistics, embedded operating services and a network of riders support customer relationships. Counterevidence: manpower services face large organised competitors, customer volumes are not committed, and software revenue is too small to justify a platform monopoly premium.

REV.reason: Constant-parent FY23–FY26 operating revenue CAGR is 32.62%, mapping to 9 but capped at 8 for the three-year comparable history. FY23–FY25 are restated and FY26 uses the parent, not acquired group revenue. Counterevidence: the latest year accelerates sharply after a nearly flat FY25, top-ten customer concentration is 81.76% at group scope, parent related-party business can change with acquisitions, and the older five-year statutory-to-restated bridge is incomplete. The 51.37% five-year statutory diagnostic is not the scoring baseline.

DUR.reason: Recurring diagnostic collection and outsourced operating needs support a continuing service market; a large partner and field-workforce network provides a route to expansion. Counterevidence: top-ten customers contribute 81.76%, no minimum volumes protect demand, and payroll-led growth requires cash before collection.

CAP.reason: The IPO funds identifiable working capital, machinery and debt repayment; acquisitions add service capability rather than a purely financial portfolio. Counterevidence: receivables absorbed substantial cash, multiple acquisitions obscure incremental returns, and their partial-year profits are not a comparable organic ROIC series.

CASH.reason: FY24 and restated FY25 standalone CFO were positive, which argues against declaring a persistent failure. Counterevidence: FY26 consolidated CFO is negative 6.62 crore, receivables consume 28.36 crore, and cash capex leaves negative 12.14 crore FCF before acquisitions. IPO proceeds do not turn this into operating cash generation.

BAL.reason: Fresh equity and the stated debt-repayment object improve the potential funding buffer; March group debt was 21.95 crore against equity 43.79 crore. Counterevidence: most IPO cash is committed to working capital, noncurrent FD availability is not verified, and actual post-issue deployment is not yet established.

EXEC.reason: Service scale, workforce deployment and completed acquisitions show execution capacity. Counterevidence: acquired scope and concentrated clients inflate the apparent growth signal, and collection execution materially lagged reported profit. No unsupported acquisition annualisation is credited.

EARN.reason: FY26 profit remains substantial after the small disclosed FY26 restatement, and the cash bridge identifies rather than hides working-capital absorption. Counterevidence: unbilled-service approvals, prior-year timing corrections and acquired software profits lower repeatability confidence; current profit is not equivalent to distributable cash.

R.reason: NS. The conditional base IRR is about 1.2%, but actual post-IPO cash deployment, recurring acquisition contribution and future bank headroom are not verified sufficiently to adopt it as expected return. The model is a decision sensitivity, not a supported R input.

D.reason: Concentrated clients, payroll-before-collection economics and the severe no-reserve funding stress create a credible permanent-loss path. Counterevidence: fresh equity and recurring diagnostic activity reduce immediate refinancing pressure if disclosed objects and cash deployment are fulfilled.

P.reason: Hard asset support is modest relative to the dated equity value, while receivables, unbilled claims, goodwill and ringfenced IPO cash cannot all be monetised as free cash. Counterevidence: the fresh issue improves book capital and disclosed receivables are mostly recent, so a zero-recovery assumption is not justified.

L.reason: The 41 listed-session actual turnover median implies about 0.34 days to exit 5 lakh at 5% participation, a raw favourable turnover band. Reduce to 7 for the short post-IPO history, 2.04-lakh lot, fewer-than-100-PAN caution and irregular-trading flag. Two lots fit within 5 lakh; three do not. No live spread/depth or guaranteed executable exit is claimed.
